jobs.description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. About the role The Partner Engagements Manager, Compliance Strategy will lead Checkout’s external-facing compliance strategy across banking, scheme and other strategic partner relationships. You will own the operating model and delivery of compliance-related partner engagements, including annual reviews, periodic due diligence, requests for information, licensing and scheme initiatives, and readiness for product or geographic expansion. You will ensure that Checkout presents a consistent, accurate and well-evidenced view of its compliance framework, while converting external expectations into practical improvements to our roadmap, controls, processes and operating model. The role combines strategic ownership, senior stakeholder management and hands-on delivery. You will lead complex engagements, advise Compliance leadership, build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, and develop the partner-engagement capability of the team, including managing and coaching Senior Analyst(s) as the structure is established. You should be comfortable taking responsibility for your work while identifying material risks and knowing when to escalate. This individual-contributor role reports to our Associate General Counsel, EU Policy/Regulatory. Advise on the interpretation and application of existing and emerging AI, digital and technology regulation, and translate complex regulatory requirements into practical legal and business guidance. Assess regulatory developments, enforcement risks and policy proposals, and develop legal recommendations for the AGC on their implications for OpenAI’s products and operations. jobs.description: About the Role A legal technology company is seeking a Germany-based Senior Partner to help grow an AI-enabled legal practice. You will bring an established client portfolio, continue advising those clients, and work with the team to move recurring legal matters onto AI-assisted workflows. What You'll Do Bring your portable client portfolio to the firm and continue serving those clients. Build relationships with private equity, venture capital, and mid-market clients to support business development. Identify opportunities to provide commercial and compliance services across your client network. Work with the founding team to assess and automate recurring legal matters using AI tools and agent-based workflows. Help shape the firm's growth and represent its legal services in the market. What We're Looking For 12 to 20 or more years of German legal practice, including experience at partner level. A German-qualified Volljurist admitted as a Rechtsanwalt, with native-level German and professional English. A personally held, portable book of business valued at €1 million or more, with a diversified client base and relationships that can transition with you. Experience serving private equity or venture capital clients and their portfolio companies, with recurring work in areas such as commercial contracts, IT and data, corporate matters, or regulatory compliance. Practical experience using AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, or legal AI products, and a demonstrated interest in updating legal workflows through automation. Ability to work in Germany and a feasible path to transition your client work. Compensation & Benefits Base salary: €200,000 to €300,000 annually. The role includes meaningful equity.
